CAP-08.why: Québec's requirement for a written final response within 60-90 days, and Florida's 455.225(9) mandated status notifications to complainants, make complaint correspondence binding and externally consequential, matching band 70 rather than routine internal documents.

CAP-10.why: Statutory deadlines (Colorado's 240-day goal, Québec's 60/90-day cap, Florida's 10-day broker notification) impose strict, auditable timelines where missed deadlines are reportable regulatory events, matching band 70 rather than a discretionary internal procedure.

CAP-10.why: Multiple statutory regimes (Colorado 240-day investigation goal, Québec 60/90-day response deadline, RERA 60-day disposal requirement, Florida notification triggers) impose strict procedural deadlines and notification duties whose breach is a reportable regulatory event, matching band 70 rather than general adherence at band 50.

evidence.regime: Real estate complaint handling and consumer protection regulations across multiple jurisdictions

sources.title: Colorado Real Estate Division Complaint Process Regulations
sources.rule: Respondent notification and response requirement; 240-day investigation completion goal
sources.cite: Colorado Division of Real Estate regulations

sources.title: Regulation on Complaint Handling in Québec's Financial Sector
sources.rule: Final response must be provided in writing within 60 days, or maximum 90 days if exceptional circumstances apply; complaint summary must be posted on website in easily identifiable location
sources.cite: Québec financial sector complaint handling regulation

sources.title: The Complaint Handling Code
sources.rule: Landlords must comply with statutory complaint handling code requirements; annual submissions and self-assessments required

sources.title: Florida Statutes Section 455.225(9)
sources.rule: DBPR must notify person who filed complaint of investigation status, probable cause finding, and administrative proceeding or appeal status

sources.title: Florida Statutes Section 475.25(5)
sources.rule: Buyer or seller has five years to file administrative complaint against broker or broker associate after act occurs or is discovered

sources.title: Florida Statutes Section 475.25(6)
sources.rule: Broker must be notified in writing about complaint against sales associate within 10 days after probable cause finding or when associate waives confidentiality privilege

sources.title: Florida Statutes Section 475.25(1)
sources.rule: Maximum administrative fine FREC may impose is $5,000 for each count or separate offense

sources.title: Real Estate Regulation Act (RERA)
sources.rule: Real estate regulatory authority must dispose of application within 60 days from date of receiving it

sources.title: French Law No. 70-9 of January 2, 1970
sources.rule: Regulates conditions for carrying out activities relating to transactions involving immovable property

sources.title: French Decree No. 72-678 of 20 July 1972
sources.rule: Obligation to hold a warrant (Article 73) for real estate professionals

sources.title: French Order of 10 January 2017
sources.rule: Requires information for consumers by professionals involved in real estate transaction

sources.title: FCA Consumer Duty Regulation
sources.rule: Firms must ensure customers with characteristics of vulnerability receive outcomes as good as other customers and must tailor products, services, communications and support accordingly

sources.title: UK GDPR Article 30
sources.rule: Organizations with more than 250 employees and smaller organizations processing data regularly must maintain written record of all data processing activities
